Commonwealth Games live updates: Athletics stars hit the track and field, Australia's pool domination continues
It's day four of the Commonwealth Games and that means the athletics program starts, marking the first of three days that feature swimming as well as track and field.
Australia's much-hyped sprint stars will hit the track in the men's and women's 100m heats while golden girls Mollie O'Callaghan, Shayna Jack and Meg Harris will fight it out in the 100m freestyle final.
Follow all the action in our live blog.

Mon 27 Jul 2026 at 7:57pm
Swimming: Three Aussies into the 400IM final
The 400 IM is the great test of a swimmer's overall skill - and it's a brutal test.
The greatest swimmer in the world, Summer McIntosh, is unfortunately not here at these Games, opting to keep her powder dry for the Pan Pacs in California next month.
Jenna Forrester is a joy of a swimmer to watch, so languid and easy in the way she moves through the water in the first two legs, particularly the backstroke.
Teammate Ella Ramsay closed her down a bit over the breaststroke, but it was Forrester who claimed the win in heat two.
Tara Kinder came second in her heat, swimming 4:41.81 behind heat winner Amalie Smith of England, who is just 16 years old, and flew through in a 4:39.13 to claim the fastest qualifying time.
Mon 27 Jul 2026 at 7:49pm
The Sun is trying its best
It's a very grey, cold, mizzly day at Scotstoun as the Games' only outdoor event kicks off.
Some sunshine is occasional lightening things up but not much. Runners are gonna be cold and wet and just going to have to deal with it.
We're smack bang on the finish line up here.
Mon 27 Jul 2026 at 7:47pm
First Aussie hits the track at Scotstoun Stadium
Heat 7 of the men's 100m sprint is on now!
We're looking at the green and gold in lane 8, Rohan Browning.
And they're off!
Browning is flying ahead, and he's crossed the line second - C'MON AUSSIE!
Mon 27 Jul 2026 at 7:45pm
Swimming: Harrison Turner qualifies fastest for 200m fly
Great swim for Harrison Turner in the 200m butterfly.
He went in the final heat and blew the rest of the field away with a very impressive performance.
Matt Temple did not look quite so good unfortunately, his time of 1:59.06 just sneaking him into the final in eighth place. That's a bit of a comedown from the 100 success but he has to be happy to be in another final.
Se-Bom Lee, unfortunately, missed out on the final with a 2:00.60.
New Zealand's Lewis Clareburt qualified second-fastest.
Mon 27 Jul 2026 at 7:44pm
Meet the Aussie sprinters up first today
Rohan Browning and Edward Nketia will compete in the men's 100m sprint soon - there's 11 heats happening at Scotstoun Stadium tonight, we're in the 7th and 11th races.
Our boys be eyeing the 23-year-old record time of 9.93s, which was set by Aussie sprint star Patrick Johnson.
No Australian has won this event, or its predecessor (the 100y, as it was known), since the Auckland Commonwealth Games in 1950.
The last time we secured a medal in the men's 100m was at the 1962 Commonwealth Games in Perth, when Michael Cleary claimed bronze.
Browning is just setting up on the starting line now, c'mon green and gold!

new_text:
Commonwealth Games updates: Australia continues to dominate the pool, gymnasts get in on the medal action
Mollie O'Callaghan has been sensationally dethroned as Commonwealth Games 100m freestyle champion by Meg Harris as Australia's tsunami of swimming medals continued in Glasgow.
Harris's shock triumph came after Jenna Forrester extended her brilliant meet with a second gold medal, adding the 400m individual medley title to her 200m backstroke crown.
O'Callaghan had been expected to again battle through the pain barrier to defend her crown but instead had to settle for the silver in another Australian 1-2-3, as Shayna Jack, in her final competition, grabbed the bronze.
But this time, it was Albury's Harris, the 24-year-old double Olympic relay champion, who had the measure of the five-time Olympic winner, leading her at the halfway mark, with O'Callaghan turning in third.
The Queensland star could not peg back the lead as Harris touched the wall in 52.90 seconds to O'Callaghan's 53.25 and Jack's 53.38.
"Very happy. Look, I wasn't meant to be here," O'Callaghan told reporters.
"So, to be on the podium with these two amazing ladies; Meg absolute killed it tonight, so did Shayna. Like, honestly, I'm just so happy."
Alex Perkins marked her 26th birthday with a perfect present as she lifted the 100m butterfly crown, her second triumph in three days after years of near-misses at major individual international events.
Perkins continues to enjoy the most extraordinary meet, winning her fourth gold in as many nights, and on a landmark day.
The 50m fly champion was in a different class from her chasers, stopping the clock at 56.38, with Scotland's Keanna MacInnes second, almost a second behind.
Sam Williamson, already champion in the 100m, again upset the odds to produce a thunderous late burst to get up for gold in the 50m breaststroke dash.
Williamson's charge for the wall in the one-lap breaststroke was one of the highlights of the meet as he powered through the second half of the race to prevail in 26.50, 0.27sec clear of South African Michael Houlie and 0.44 ahead of English Olympic great Adam Ramsay-Peaty.
Para swimmer Beau Matthews added another gold in the 100m breaststroke SB9 final, while Sam Short powered home to win the 800m freestyle final.
Matthews, seen as a future para star, came of age, clocking 1:09.41 to better Tim Hodge, Australia's baton bearer at the opening ceremony.
Hodge, who had won the 100m backstroke S9 the night before, had to settle for bronze behind New Zealander Joshua Willmer.
'Don't be poo': McDonald quells doubts with gold
Fighting off the voices in her head that tell her "don't be poo", Kate McDonald won Australia's second gymnastics gold medal at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games.
It was sweet redemption for McDonald, who banished haunting memories of her "pretty poo" finish at the 2022 Birmingham Games with a near-flawless performance at Glasgow International Stadium, scoring 14.333 points.
So dominant was the 25-year-old that she was the only gymnast to hit the 14.000-point mark and blitzed next-best, Canadian great Ellie Black, by 0.433 points, with Wales's Emily Roper following for bronze.
"I'm over the moon," McDonald said.
"I bombed in that (2022) final, and that's obviously in the back of my head.
"I did want this medal really badly."
Wearing her headphones during warm-up, McDonald said cycling through her competition playlist - from AC/DC to Dom Dolla - helped her fight off memories of the 2022 final.
Whether a coincidence or a good omen in her 2028 Los Angeles qualifying campaign, her final song before competing was a remix of California Dreamin'.
"Putting music in helps ground me, and that helps the voice in my head stay nice," McDonald said.
"''Don't be poo, don't fall. Be perfect, it's not going to be perfect.' There's a lot of background noise.
"I'm just going to again try and learn from this experience and bring it into LA; hopefully, we qualify a team for LA, hopefully I'm on that team for LA."
As McDonald led the charge in the women's field, James Hardy claimed bronze on the rings and the floor routine exercise.
Just as the team bronze was Australia's first since the 2010 Delhi Games, Hardy's two individual bronze medals ended the nation's 16-year drought on the apparatuses in the men's field.
The 23-year-old competed with a pink ribbon painted on the nail of his right hand ring finger in tribute to his mum, Sally, who has breast cancer.
She is in remission after undergoing surgery, but she and the Hardy family were unable to travel to Glasgow.
"It's been in the back of my mind, but obviously nice to know that she's just doing really well," Hardy said.
"Spoken to mum and dad before, they're absolutely, you know, just so, so, so proud.
"It's very emotional. They would have loved to be here."
Catch up on all the action from day four of the games in our blog below.

Tue 28 Jul 2026 at 7:27am
WHAT A FINISH AT THE MEN'S 79KG
Well Rory Scott might have been out but I hope you stayed tuned in to the men's 79kg weightlifting because Erry Hidayat Muhammad and Valluri Ajaya Babu just chucked metaphorical haymakers at each other for an incredible finish.
The pair set back-to-back-to-back Commonwealth Games records in the run home.
India's Babu blasted 181kg to sit in gold medal spot and throw the challenge to Malaysia's Muhammad to come and take it.
With his last lift, Muhammad went all the way up to 184kg - another Games record - and dug deep to get the three green lights and snatch the win.
Babu takes home the silver, with Englishman Chris Murray in third.
Thrilling stuff!
Tue 28 Jul 2026 at 7:17am
Need a catch up? We got you
Maybe you're just waking up or you're on your way to work via public transport and you're desperate to find out what happened overnight and this morning.
Here's what you need to know as the ABC Sport desk work allll the way through the night to bring you all the action from Glasgow:
- Gymnast Kate McDonald won a glorious gold on the uneven bars
- James Hardy had a sensational day, coming away with two bronze gymnastics medals, one on floor and one on the rings
- Sprinter Rohan Browning slammed the qualifying system saying "it's not fair"
- Heartbreaking injury forced Breanna Mae Kean out of the women's 53kg weightlifting
And don't forget our domination in the pool and our first athletics medal, which was a gold!

Aussie Paul Trainor won his men's 80kg round-of-16 fight 3-2 against Namibian Gebhard Tonateni Ipinge.
That means he will take on Welshman Daniel Pitt in the quarterfinals on Thursday morning around 5:45am AEST.
